absent: Locking, concurrency and interrupt safety for init tables, hypercalls and event helpers are not shown.
Implementations behind all function pointer tables and their call order across boot phases are not shown.
Numeric hypervisor operation codes, multicall entry layout and trap, MMU, descriptor and page table record layouts are not shown.
VMX short report names, MSR encodings and hardware checking of capability bits are not shown.
Error codes, retry rules and failure handling for hypercalls and encryption status changes are not shown.
Register frame, CPU info, IRQ domain, clock and hypervisor shared page layouts are not shown.

findings.text: Secondary virtualization capability numbers begin at 64. The routed range assigns 64 to VMX_FEATURE_VIRT_APIC_ACCESSES, 65 to VMX_FEATURE_EPT, 66 to VMX_FEATURE_DESC_EXITING, 67 to VMX_FEATURE_RDTSCP, 68 to VMX_FEATURE_VIRTUAL_X2APIC, 69 to VMX_FEATURE_VPID, 70 to VMX_FEATURE_WBINVD_EXITING, 71 to VMX_FEATURE_UNRESTRICTED_GUEST, 72 to VMX_FEATURE_APIC_REGISTER_VIRT, 73 to VMX_FEATURE_VIRT_INTR_DELIVERY, 74 to VMX_FEATURE_PAUSE_LOOP_EXITING, 75 to VMX_FEATURE_RDRAND_EXITING and 76 to VMX_FEATURE_INVPCID.

Higher secondary numbers continue with 77 for VMX_FEATURE_VMFUNC, 78 for VMX_FEATURE_SHADOW_VMCS, 79 for VMX_FEATURE_ENCLS_EXITING, 80 for VMX_FEATURE_RDSEED_EXITING, 81 for VMX_FEATURE_PAGE_MOD_LOGGING, 82 for VMX_FEATURE_EPT_VIOLATION_VE, 83 for VMX_FEATURE_PT_CONCEAL_VMX, 84 for VMX_FEATURE_XSAVES, 86 for VMX_FEATURE_MODE_BASED_EPT_EXEC, 88 for VMX_FEATURE_PT_USE_GPA, 89 for VMX_FEATURE_TSC_SCALING, 90 for VMX_FEATURE_USR_WAIT_PAUSE, 92 for VMX_FEATURE_ENCLV_EXITING, 94 for VMX_FEATURE_BUS_LOCK_DETECTION and 95 for VMX_FEATURE_NOTIFY_VM_EXITING. Values 85, 87, 91 and 93 are not defined in the routed range. Tertiary number 100 selects VMX_FEATURE_IPI_VIRT.

Legacy vsyscall support is fully disabled in this configuration. The helper named map_vsyscall performs no action and the helpers named emulate_vsyscall_pf and emulate_vsyscall_gp always report failure. Callers must treat the false result as no emulation and continue with normal fault handling without expecting register or memory changes.

The record named word_at_a_time holds two machine words named one_bits and high_bits. A constant initializer fills them with repeated low and high byte patterns derived from byte values 0x01 and 0x80 across the whole word. The values are read only inputs for later zero byte tests.

Zero byte detection operates on one machine word at a time using helpers named has_zero, prep_zero_mask, create_zero_mask, zero_bytemask and find_zero. The first helper computes a marker mask for bytes that may be zero and returns it while also storing it through an output pointer. The second helper forwards an existing marker unchanged. Two target variants then either pass the marker through and derive a full byte mask plus first zero location, or first derive the byte mask and then locate the first zero with endian specific arithmetic. All steps are pure register arithmetic with no memory access.

Early platform dispatch is split by subsystem. The table named x86_init_mpparse offers setup_ioapic_ids, find_mptable, early_parse_smp_cfg and parse_smp_cfg. The table named x86_init_resources offers probe_roms, reserve_resources, memory_setup and dmi_setup plus a realmode_limit value. The table named x86_init_irqs offers pre_vector_init, intr_init, intr_mode_select and intr_mode_init plus create_pci_msi_domain. The table named x86_init_oem offers arch_setup and banner. The table named x86_init_paging offers pagetable_init. The table named x86_init_timers offers setup_percpu_clockev, timer_init and wallclock_init. The table named x86_init_iommu offers iommu_init. The table named x86_init_pci offers arch_init, init, init_irq and fixup_irqs.

Hypervisor and firmware dispatch covers three small tables. The table named x86_hyper_init offers init_platform, guest_late_init, x2apic_available, msi_ext_dest_id, init_mem_mapping and init_after_bootmem. The table named x86_init_acpi offers set_root_pointer, get_root_pointer and reduced_hw_early_init. The table named x86_guest offers enc_status_change_prepare, enc_status_change_finish, enc_tlb_flush_required, enc_cache_flush_required, enc_kexec_begin and enc_kexec_finish.

The table named x86_init_ops aggregates resource, MP parse, interrupt, OEM, paging, timer, IOMMU, PCI, hypervisor and ACPI groups as named members. The table named x86_cpuinit_ops offers setup_percpu_clockev, early_percpu_clock_init and fixup_cpu_id plus a parallel_bringup flag controlling concurrent startup.

Legacy and runtime platform state uses compact records. The record named x86_legacy_devices holds a pnpbios indicator. The enumeration named x86_legacy_i8042_state distinguishes platform absent, firmware absent and expected present. The record named x86_legacy_features combines that i8042 state with rtc, warm reset, VGA absence and BIOS region reservation indicators plus the device record. The table named x86_hyper_runtime offers pin_vcpu, sev_es_hcall_prepare, sev_es_hcall_finish and is_private_mmio. The table named x86_platform_ops offers CPU and TSC calibration, wall clock access, IOMMU shutdown, PAT range checks, NMI handling, scheduler clock save and restore, APIC post init, legacy handling, real mode handling and nested hypervisor and guest groups. The table named x86_apic_ops offers IO APIC read and restore.

Xen CPUID identification uses XEN_CPUID_FIRST_LEAF at hexadecimal 40000000 with XEN_CPUID_LEAF adding small indices to address further leaves. Signature words are XEN_CPUID_SIGNATURE_EBX at hexadecimal 566E6558 in EBX, XEN_CPUID_SIGNATURE_ECX at hexadecimal 65584D4D in ECX and XEN_CPUID_SIGNATURE_EDX at hexadecimal 4D4D566E in EDX. Feature word one uses _XEN_CPUID_FEAT1_MMU_PT_UPDATE_PRESERVE_AD at index zero and XEN_CPUID_FEAT1_MMU_PT_UPDATE_PRESERVE_AD at mask one for preservation of accessed and dirty information across page table updates.

TSC behavior uses XEN_CPUID_TSC_EMULATED at bit zero, XEN_CPUID_HOST_TSC_RELIABLE at bit one and XEN_CPUID_RDTSCP_INSTR_AVAIL at bit two. Mode selection uses XEN_CPUID_TSC_MODE_DEFAULT at zero, XEN_CPUID_TSC_MODE_ALWAYS_EMULATE at one, XEN_CPUID_TSC_MODE_NEVER_EMULATE at two and XEN_CPUID_TSC_MODE_PVRDTSCP at three. HVM controls use XEN_HVM_CPUID_APIC_ACCESS_VIRT at bit zero, XEN_HVM_CPUID_X2APIC_VIRT at bit one, XEN_HVM_CPUID_IOMMU_MAPPINGS at bit two, XEN_HVM_CPUID_VCPU_ID_PRESENT at bit three, XEN_HVM_CPUID_DOMID_PRESENT at bit four, XEN_HVM_CPUID_EXT_DEST_ID at bit five and XEN_HVM_CPUID_UPCALL_VECTOR at bit six. Machine address width uses XEN_CPUID_MACHINE_ADDRESS_WIDTH_MASK over the low eight bits and XEN_CPUID_MAX_NUM_LEAVES limits leaf count to five.

The enumeration named ipi_vector orders reschedule, call function, call function single, spin unlock, IRQ work and NMI vectors followed by a count sentinel. The order defines the numeric values used by event dispatch.

The helper named xen_irqs_disabled reports disabled state from saved processor flags. The helper named xchg_xen_ulong forwards to an atomic exchange primitive. The helper named xen_support_evtchn_rebind reports support on non HVM guests and on HVM guests only when vector callbacks are enabled.

Xen hypercalls invoke a static call trampoline named __HYPERCALL with the operation number in the accumulator. Thirty two bit builds place result and five arguments in EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI and EDI. Sixty four bit builds use RAX, RDI, RSI, RDX, R10 and R8. Fixed register declarations named __HYPERCALL_DECLS with per arity argument assignment, output marking and clobber lists cover zero to five arguments with memory always clobbered and unused argument registers listed as clobbered.

The helper named xen_single_call accepts an operation number plus five machine words and returns the hypervisor result word. The wrapper named privcmd_call invokes the same path while briefly suppressing access checks and then restoring them. Two tiny helpers implement the suppress and restore steps with memory and flag clobbers in a form hidden from static tooling.

Direct hypercall wrappers named HYPERVISOR_set_trap_table, HYPERVISOR_mmu_update, HYPERVISOR_mmuext_op, HYPERVISOR_set_gdt, HYPERVISOR_callback_op, HYPERVISOR_set_debugreg, HYPERVISOR_get_debugreg, HYPERVISOR_update_descriptor, HYPERVISOR_update_va_mapping and HYPERVISOR_set_segment_base forward to generic builders with matching arity. Batch forms carry request pointer, count, success count pointer and domain identifier. Mapping update carries address, entry value and flags.

Multicall builders named MULTI_fpu_taskswitch, MULTI_update_va_mapping, MULTI_update_descriptor, MULTI_mmu_update and MULTI_mmuext_op fill an entry with an operation code and ordered arguments then record a trace event with the argument count. Argument counts are one, three, two, four and four respectively with ordering matching the direct wrappers.

Routed headers each define a single inclusion guard macro named _ASM_X86_VSYSCALL_H, _ASM_WORD_AT_A_TIME_H, _ASM_X86_PLATFORM_H, __XEN_PUBLIC_ARCH_X86_CPUID_H__, _ASM_X86_XEN_EVENTS_H and _ASM_X86_XEN_HYPERCALL_H that prevents multiple inclusion. The guards carry no runtime behavior and only control preprocessing.

Legacy keyboard controller presence uses enumeration x86_legacy_i8042_state with three mutually exclusive values for platform absent, firmware absent and expected present, selected once by platform detection. TSC virtualization mode uses four mutually exclusive selections for default, always emulate, never emulate and paravirtual RDTSCP, qualified by separate capability bits for emulation and reliability.

Caller hazards center on short protection windows and strict ordering. The privileged path briefly lifts access checks and must always restore them without intervening faults. Multicall slots require operation code first and exact arity or later arguments are misread. Disabled vsyscall emulation must not be mistaken for success. Word scan helpers require the matching endian variant or byte positions are wrong.
Interrupt flag evaluation delegates to an external helper owned by another dossier.
